name: Fieldnote
tagline: Simple time tracking and invoicing for freelancers
home: Fieldnote is a time tracker for freelancers and small studios. Start a timer from your menu bar, tag the client and project, and turn tracked hours into an invoice in two clicks.
It works on Mac, Windows and the web, syncs between devices, and exports to CSV for your accountant.
about: Fieldnote is made by two designers who were tired of spreadsheets and missed billable hours.
It costs $8 a month after a 14-day free trial, with no limit on clients or projects.

posts.title: How to track billable hours without losing time
posts.description: Habits that make sure every billable minute ends up on an invoice.
posts.body:
Most freelancers lose billable time in small pieces: a five-minute email here, a quick call there.

## Start the timer before you start the work

Make it a habit: open the task, start the timer, then begin.

## Tag as you go

Tag client and project when you start, not at the end of the week when you've forgotten.

## Review every Friday

Ten minutes on Friday to fix gaps saves an afternoon at the end of the month.

posts.title: Hourly vs project pricing for freelancers
posts.description: When each pricing model works, and how to switch.
posts.body:
Hourly pricing is fair when the scope is unclear. Project pricing rewards you for working efficiently.

## Charge hourly when

The client keeps changing the brief, or the work is support and maintenance.

## Charge per project when

You've done similar work many times and can estimate it well.

## Use your tracked hours

Your past time logs are the best guide to what a project price should be.
